# Assumption Registry

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/assumptions.mjs — do not edit by hand.

Every product bet embedded in the code, made visible so it can be reviewed
against **docs/PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md**.

**How to use this in an audit:** read each row and ask *"is this still true for
the customer we actually have?"* — not *"is this code correct?"*. The
`country: "us"` default that hid the Mumbai One bug for months was correct
code and a wrong bet. Only this question finds that class of defect.

4 assumptions found.

| Where | We are betting that… | If wrong… |
|---|---|---|
| `src/lib/storefronts.ts:29` | Our customers' apps live in the US, India or UK storefronts | an app published only in e.g. Brazil or Indonesia is unfindable and syncs zero reviews — exactly the Mumbai One failure, one country over |
| `src/services/bootstrap-reviews.ts:21` | 200 recent reviews is enough history for a new workspace | a high-volume app shows only a few days of reviews and looks broken to its owner |
| `src/services/bootstrap-reviews.ts:76` | Customers only care about English-language reviews | a Hindi/Marathi-heavy app (our ICP) shows a fraction of its real feedback |
| `src/services/store-search.ts:46` | A 6-hour-old rating is fresh enough to show as current | after a rating spike the dashboard contradicts the store for up to 6 hours |
